title: Project: Password Meter
story: The post office wants a quick strength meter for new passwords.
goal: Read a password. Score 1 point each for: 8+ characters, a digit, an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter. 4 points: strong, 2 or 3: medium, otherwise weak.
starter:
pw = input()
# score the password and print weak, medium or strong
hints: Keep a score variable and add 1 for each rule that holds. any(...) can check characters.
any(ch.isdigit() for ch in pw) is True when there is a digit. isupper and islower work the same way.
socratic: How do you check whether any character is a digit?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the key idea in “Project: Password Meter”?
alt:
pw = input()
rules = [len(pw) >= 8, any(c.isdigit() for c in pw), any(c.isupper() for c in pw), any(c.islower() for c in pw)]
score = sum(rules)
print("strong" if score == 4 else "medium" if score >= 2 else "weak")
